description: We are a team of six passionate students participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We have formed our team to work on the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge. Our goal is to build an interactive, space-themed educational game that helps students understand space exploration, resource management, and the challenges astronauts face during missions. We look forward to collaborating, learning, and developing our solution together.
summary:
Mission Void — Explore. Build. Survive.

Mission Void is an immersive space exploration and survival game that takes players beyond Earth and into the challenges of building a sustainable human presence on the Moon. The journey begins at a small lunar outpost, where players take on the role of an astronaut responsible for exploring unfamiliar terrain, completing scientific missions, and gradually developing a fully functional lunar base.

Every decision matters. Players must manage essential resources such as energy, oxygen, and food while maintaining equipment, expanding habitats, and preparing for unexpected challenges. From collecting lunar soil samples and studying surface conditions to investigating water ice, monitoring solar radiation, and operating exploration rovers, each mission introduces a new challenge inspired by real aspects of space research.

As players complete missions, they earn rewards, unlock upgrades, and expand their settlement with new facilities and technologies. However, progress requires careful planning, as limited resources and unpredictable lunar conditions can put the entire base at risk.

More than just a space adventure, Mission Void aims to make space science engaging through interactive gameplay. It combines exploration, strategy, survival, and scientific discovery to help players understand the complexities of living beyond Earth.

The mission is simple: explore the unknown, build a future, and survive beyond Earth.
details:
MISSION VOID — VEYRA: Sustain Life Beyond Earth

MISSION VOID is an interactive 3D lunar survival and settlement simulation that places players in the role of a commander tasked with establishing a sustainable human presence on the Moon. Players begin with a single habitat module and gradually transform it into a functioning lunar settlement by exploring the lunar surface, completing missions, collecting resources and making critical engineering decisions.

The experience is structured across six chapters and 30 missions, taking players from their first lunar survival challenges to developing the infrastructure needed for a sustainable settlement and exploring technologies relevant to future Mars missions. Players operate rovers, collect and analyse lunar regolith samples, complete optional side quests and manage essential resources such as oxygen, power, water, food, construction materials and science points. Each resource has a purpose, and players must plan carefully before constructing or upgrading facilities.

As the settlement develops, players can build and upgrade systems such as solar arrays, battery storage, greenhouses and water recyclers. Environmental challenges, including lunar dust and solar storms, introduce additional risks. Players must decide how to use limited resources: repair damaged equipment, conserve energy, protect life-support systems or prioritise essential infrastructure. Rather than relying on sudden game-over situations, the simulation encourages players to understand the consequences of their decisions and learn through engineering trade-offs.

Benefits and intended impact: VEYRA makes the complex challenges of living beyond Earth more accessible through interactive learning. It helps students and space enthusiasts understand why life-support systems, resource efficiency, energy management, environmental protection and sustainable infrastructure are essential for lunar exploration. By allowing players to experiment with decisions and observe their consequences, the project aims to build curiosity about space science, systems engineering and the technologies needed for long-duration human missions. Its broader intended impact is to encourage interest in sustainable space exploration and the preparation required for future missions to the Moon and Mars.

Tools and technologies: The project was developed using JavaScript, React, Three.js, WebGL and Tailwind CSS. React manages the user interface, Three.js and WebGL power the interactive 3D lunar environment, and JavaScript handles the mission progression, resource management and simulation logic. The project also includes an ORION voice companion to guide players, a habitat interior view and a NASA Open Data panel presenting information from public sources such as Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), NASA's DONKI space-weather data and the NASA Image and Video Library. The NASA information is provided for learning and exploration and does not directly control gameplay.

Creativity and innovation: VEYRA combines a playable survival simulation with an evolving 3D lunar settlement. Instead of presenting space exploration as a collection of facts or static diagrams, it lets players experience the decisions involved in building and maintaining a lunar base. The settlement visibly changes as players construct and upgrade facilities, making their progress tangible. The combination of mission-based storytelling, rover exploration, resource management, optional side quests, environmental challenges and an interactive voice companion creates a more engaging way to explore lunar habitation.

Factors considered during development: Our team focused on making the experience educational, engaging and understandable while keeping the challenges meaningful. We considered the scarcity of resources, the importance of maintaining life-support systems, the effects of the lunar environment, the need to prioritise infrastructure and the consequences of engineering decisions. We also considered player progression and clarity: starting with only one habitat module gives players a clear objective, while missions and side quests guide them towards new construction and upgrades. Visual feedback helps players understand what their decisions achieve, and the NASA Open Data panel provides additional opportunities to explore real space-related information.

Through VEYRA, MISSION VOID aims to turn the challenge of sustaining human life beyond Earth into an interactive learning experience—one where every mission, resource and engineering decision contributes to building a future on the Moon.
